gaps.note: THESE BAY DIMENSIONS WERE GROWN TO MEET A COMPONENT AND ARE NOT MEASUREMENTS. Each was set by taking the size of a card the bay accepts, because a fit check reported the bay as too small. On this chassis: 42.67 on 10 bays - a9k-4hg-flex, 42.67 thick 403.40 on 10 bays - a99-rsp-se, 403.40 long 492.10 on 5 bays - a99-sfc3-s, 492.10 long The danger is specific and it is why they are listed rather than left to look like geometry. A fit check compares a bay to a component and NEITHER of them to the world, so it is satisfied by both being wrong together exactly as easily as by both being right. Every mismatch resolved by moving one side removes the signal without adding any truth, and once resolved nothing will flag it again. These are the entries where that happened, so the record survives the check going quiet. What IS independently grounded and is not in this list: the cage extents, measured off the stencil and confirmed on several chassis by printed slot labels or a card guide rail; the slot pitch; the 395.70 fourth-generation envelope, which is Cisco's own "includes ejector bracket/lever" figure; and the shapesheet sizes for the power modules and fan trays. The ejector arithmetic that explains why a bay legitimately exceeds its cage opening - 355.60 against 395.70, 40.10 mm - is also sourced, and it justifies the SHAPE of these numbers without justifying any particular one of them.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned figure giving the clear opening of any ASR 9000 card cage, which would replace every reconciled figure above with a measured one

gaps.note: A THIRD LINE OF EVIDENCE ON THE ~428 mm CONTROL CARDS, derived rather than asserted, and it comes from parts that have nothing to do with the question. The vertical space available to a card is bounded by whatever structure sits above and below its cage, and on this chassis that space measures the figure recorded in card-envelope-headroom below. A card envelope larger than that cannot be installed whatever any data sheet says, because something else is already there. Applied across the family: ASR 9010 399.96 mm between the cable management tray and the card guide bar ASR 9910 421.79 mm between the tray band and the front air intake ASR 9922 420.30 mm between the tray band and the fan band ASR 9912 439.21 mm - does NOT exclude 428.5, so this chassis is silent on the question ASR 9906 unbounded above in the model, so no constraint is derivable Three of the five independently exclude a 428.2-428.5 card. That is a separate argument from the slot pitch and from the ejector arithmetic, and it agrees with both. THE 9912 DOES NOT EXCLUDE IT and is recorded as silent rather than as agreement - a constraint that fails to bite is not evidence either way, and reporting it as if it were would manufacture support. The 9010's 399.96 also sits 3.14 mm under the 403.10 fifth-generation envelope its bays now carry, which is a smaller open question of the same kind.
gaps.wanted: a figure dimensioning the clear vertical opening of any ASR 9000 card cage, which would turn all of this from derived to measured

gaps.note: THE SECOND AXIS OF THE SAME CONFLICT, and it makes the first one much harder to explain away. The RSP-880 family is published at 428.5 mm on its long axis. Two Cisco statements fix what a line card measures on that axis in this family: Table A-10 of OL-17500-09 gives the original-generation card 14 in (355.60 mm) with NO qualifier, and the 4th-generation data sheets give 15.58 in (395.70) explicitly "including ejector bracket/lever". The 40.10 mm between them is the ejectors, about 20 mm each end - which is also why a bay declared at the 395.70 envelope is legitimately longer than the cage opening it sits in. Against that, 428.50 does not reconcile. Subtract the same 40.10 of ejector and the plate would still be 33.45 mm longer than this chassis's measured cage - a cage independently confirmed to 0.65 mm by Table A-10's own 355.60. So BOTH published RSP-880 dimensions, 46.0 thick and 428.5 long, are irreconcilable with a cage that two unrelated sources agree on. That is why the bays were NOT inflated to hold it. Building five chassis around a pair of numbers that contradict the only independently confirmed dimension in the family would put the error into the geometry instead of into the record. The accepts keep the RSP-880 where Cisco names it; the bays stay at what the cage and the reconcilable envelopes allow.
gaps.wanted: the RSP-880's plate dimensions as distinct from whatever 46.0 x 428.5 measures, or a photograph of an RSP-880 beside a line card

gaps.note: Cisco's RSP-880 and RSP880-LT data sheet gives "Height: 1.81 in. (4.60 cm)", i.e. 46.0 mm, and names the ASR 9006, 9010, 9904, 9906 and 9910 as the chassis they are the system processor for. THAT WIDTH EXCEEDS THE MEASURED SLOT PITCH ON EVERY CHASSIS IN THE FAMILY: 9010 44.33 9906 43.42 9910 43.78 9912 44.06 9922 44.06 and three of those pitches are measured from PRINTED SLOT LABELS or a card guide rail with a spread of 0.11 to 0.20 mm - among the best-supported numbers in this library. A card cannot be thicker than its slot, so 1.81 in is not the seating width; it is most likely taken over the ejector levers, the same way Cisco's line card "Width" is stated as "includes ejector bracket/lever" elsewhere. The accepts lists keep the RSP-880 family where Cisco names it, because a compatibility claim is Cisco's to make. The bays are sized to what the measured opening can hold. So a reader will find a bay narrower than a component it accepts, and that is a RECORDED CONFLICT between two sources rather than an oversight - the alternative was to inflate five chassis' geometry to fit one published number that three independent pitch measurements contradict.
gaps.wanted: the RSP-880's seating width as distinct from its over-ejector width, or any Cisco statement of an ASR 9000 slot pitch

gaps.note: Two power shelves are drawn as single openings rather than three module openings each. Table 15 establishes the count - "ASR 9910: Version 3 power system: Up to six AC power modules per system, three per tray" - and Figure 22 numbers them M0 to M3 for the DC system, which is four per tray, so the count itself DIFFERS BETWEEN AC AND DC on this chassis and neither figure nor table gives boundaries. The master draws both shelves populated, so a scan returns module detail rather than separators. The shelves' outer rectangles are measured and drawn.
gaps.wanted: a figure showing the power shelves empty, and a statement of the AC and DC module counts on one page

gaps.note: THE BOTTOM FACE IS EMPTY BY VERIFICATION, NOT BY OMISSION, and this is the only chassis in the Cisco family where that is still true. Its seven siblings each earn this face from a rack mounting surface strip dimensioned in their own footprint figure. FOUR ROUTES WERE TRIED HERE AND ALL FOUR FAIL: (1) Figure 12's Top View, read whole at 300 dpi, carries exactly one dimension - 17.600, the width - and no mounting offset. (2) The fraction route needs a scale, and that view has none that reconciles: 17.600 across its short axis makes its long axis 28.04 in, which is 11 percent off Table 13's 31.50 and 10 percent off its own side view's 31.266. (3) The HIG's 4-post mounting figures for this chassis are undimensioned illustrations. (4) Transferring the ASR 9906's 127.0 and 240.0 mm would cross two chassis differing by 313 mm in height, which is the sibling transfer this work has spent the session correcting. Separately and for the whole family: no bottom VIEW of any ASR 9000 chassis exists in the 78-document intake - every figure caption in all 65 PDFs was searched for "Bottom View", "underside" and "bottom of the chassis", returning zero hits. Nothing is drawn and no region names the absence. The face is correctly SIZED, so the 3D box and a rack elevation are the right shape; what is missing is a statement of what is on it, and this chassis holds at capability 2 rather than borrow a number it cannot source.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned rail or mounting-flange position for the ASR 9910 from any figure, or a way for a view to declare itself deliberately empty so empty-by-verification can count

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

a top-level `profile:` naming the device class, so that `specified` has something to judge the attrs against - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml for the classes that exist, which unlocks `specified` and with it the About panel, and comparison against other devices
ports the Nautobot exporter recognises - each port placement needs `attrs.media` and `attrs.speed` in a combination it maps - unlocks NetBox / Nautobot device-type export

provenance.air-filter: datasheet - Table 17, b-asr9k-hardware-installation-guide.pdf p228: "Cisco ASR 9910 Router - Located underneath the card cage", removed by sliding it out. The same guide adds that on the 9910 "the chassis air filter is not serviceable" in the sense that it recommends replacement rather than cleaning. Not modelled - no figure we hold dimensions it
provenance.airflow: datasheet - "Cisco ASR 9910 Router: Front-to-rear cooling path. The inlet is at the bottom front of the chassis, and the exhaust is at the upper rear", b-asr9k-overview-reference-guide.pdf p3734. The front's mesh panel at y 691.79 to 813.19 mm is that inlet; the rear's mesh panel at y 8.66 to 110.58 mm is the exhaust
provenance.bay-opening-is-the-hole-not-the-reserved: `size` on these bays is what the slot RESERVES - where a card is placed and what L33 and L34 check it against - and it is the card's own envelope, per the arbitration that a bay and its occupant carry the same size. The renderer also painted that rectangle dark, so the visible opening was drawn over sheet metal at each end of every slot. `opening` now carries the hole separately: 365.62 mm, the cage measured off the front master at y 274.22 to 639.84. NOTHING ABOUT PLACEMENT OR CHECKING MOVES. Only what is painted dark changes, and the opening is centred on the bay because a hole and the space reserved around it share a centre. Where only one axis is measured the other keeps the bay's own figure rather than being inferred from the occupant, which is the mistake this field exists to undo.
provenance.bottom-face-attempted-and-refused: measured - the fraction route was tried and it failed the gate, so it was not used. Every sibling's mounting plane came from a dimensioned figure; the 9910's Figure 12 dimensions only the overall width, height and depth. The remaining option was to measure the flange line off its top view as a FRACTION of a dimension it does state, which the skill permits. That needs the view to be orthographic, and it is not: the drawn outline measures 710 by 445 px, an aspect of 0.6268 against the 17.600 by 31.266 in it states, which is 0.5629 - out by 11.3 percent. The only interior vertical line the scan finds sits 4.5 mm from an edge, which is a skin line rather than a flange at any plausible depth. The HIG's 4-post mounting figures for this chassis are installation illustrations with no dimensions on them. So this face stays empty and this chassis stays at capability 2. A failed gate is a reason to stop, not a reason to use the broken ruler anyway - the same call casa-cards made on the ASR 9000v, and the same one this file made on Figure 12's side view earlier
provenance.bottom-face-figure-12-checked-directly: datasheet - FINAL CHECK, made because Figure 12 is the best drawing in the corpus and it was reasonable to expect it to carry this. IT DOES NOT. Its Top View is rendered at 300 dpi and read whole, with a generous crop in case a dimension had been cut off, and it carries EXACTLY ONE dimension: 17.600, the chassis width, on a vertical arrow at its right. There is no second dimension line anywhere on that view. The 31.266 "Cable Mgt to Fabric card" below it belongs to the Side View, not the Top. AND THE VIEW CANNOT BE CALIBRATED TO RECOVER IT. Taking 17.600 in across its 445 px short axis gives 0.03955 in/px, at which its 709 px long axis measures 28.04 in - against Table 13's 31.50 (-11.0%) and the side view's 31.266 (-10.3%). It matches no dimension anyone states, so there is no scale to put a fraction on. The only interior vertical line the scan finds sits about 5 mm from an edge, which is a skin or flange line at the chassis wall rather than a mounting plane at any plausible depth. So the best-documented chassis in the family does not give this, which is a real finding rather than a search that fell short: Figure 12 spends its dimensions on the OUTSIDE of the box and none on where the box mounts
provenance.calibration: measured - the best gate-1 result in the whole family. Calibrating x on 482.6 mm (the 19.0 in rack face) and y on Table 13's 932.18 mm INDEPENDENTLY gives 0.20134 and 0.20133 mm/px - they agree to 0.00 percent. Origin shifted in by (482.6 - 447.0) / 2 = 17.8 mm to reach the body
provenance.card-bays: the card openings are BAYS, converted from cutouts once cisco/a9k-slot-cover@1 was shown to fit them. That took no new component: the blank carries the line card envelope, 41.4 x 395.7, which is the same envelope every card in this cage uses, and the question that had held the conversion up - whether a component's size is its faceplate or its slot envelope - was settled as the envelope. The measured pitch is wider than the envelope by the card guide, which is chassis structure and not bay. Bays are sized to the component and positioned on the measured cage, matching every other chassis in this family
provenance.card-cage: drawing - front cage opening x 4.15 to 442.85 mm, y 274.22 to 639.84 mm. Slots are anchored on the printed label centres rather than on an even division of that span
provenance.card-envelope-headroom: derived - 421.79 mm of clear vertical space between the structure above this card cage and the structure below it, measured off this chassis's own committed geometry. Any card envelope larger than that cannot be installed regardless of what its data sheet states. Used as a check on the control-card lengths, not as a source for the bays
provenance.card-orientation: datasheet - stated directly, and it had been an inference until now. The Overview and Reference Guide's "Chassis Slots" section (b-asr9k-overview-reference-guide.pdf p17) names every chassis in the family and gives the ejector position as the tell: "Cisco ASR 9910 Router: All line cards and RSP cards are front-facing and mounted vertically, with ejector levers and captive screws at the top and bottom of each card". A bay therefore places a card component unrotated. Only the ASR 9006 and ASR 9904 are horizontal; the 9010, 9906, 9910, 9912 and 9922 all stand their cards up, including the 21 RU 9010. This section supersedes the three-way inference an earlier revision rested on - the slot figures, Figure 2's "four on each side" callout and the measured cage aspect - all of which agreed with it.
provenance.chassis: datasheet - Table 13 "Cisco ASR 9000 Series Routers Physical Descriptions", b-asr9k-overview-reference-guide.pdf p130. ASR 9910: chassis height 36.70 inches (93.28 cm), chassis width 17.6 inches (44.70 cm), chassis depth 31.50 inches (80.01 cm) "including the cable management system and front cover". Modelled as 447.0 x 932.18 x 800.1 mm
provenance.compliance: datasheet - data_sheet_c78-501767.pdf series compliance list, transcribed as printed
provenance.electrical: datasheet - Table 15 (AC) and Table 16 (DC), pp132-135, ASR 9910 columns only
provenance.environmental: datasheet - Table 14, p131. The 9910 is in the NARROWER short-term group, 23 to 122 degF (-5 to 50 degC), with the 9010, 9922 and 9912 - not the 9006/9904/9906 group's 55 degC
provenance.fabric-cage: drawing + datasheet - the REAR cage spans x 34.75 to 423.53 mm and y 270.71 to 738.01 mm and holds FIVE fabric cards. The master prints FC0 to FC4 beneath it, which is the direct source for both the count and the numbering, and Table 13 corroborates from a completely different direction: the 9910's configured weight is quoted for a chassis "Configured with two fan trays, two RSPs, five fabric cards, and one PEM". Five slots across 388.78 mm is a 77.76 mm pitch, which is roughly the label spacing of 76.4 mm
provenance.fan-trays: drawing + component - two fan trays on the REAR, between the exhaust grille and the fabric cage. Measured from the separator rules: FT0 at y 121.05 and FT1 at y 174.83, with a small "FT0 up / FT1 down" label strip between them. FT1's drawn height of 40.89 mm matches the cisco/asr-9910-fan component's stated 41.1 mm to a fifth of a millimetre, which is what justifies modelling both as REAL BAYS at the component's own size rather than at the drawn band. FT0's band measures 51.77 mm because the label strip sits inside it
provenance.four-hg-flex-accepted: datasheet - the A9K-4HG-FLEX and A99-4HG-FLEX pairs added to the line card slots, and each is placed on ITS OWN declared chassis list rather than on an inference from generation. The A9K pair's contract names all seven chassis; the A99 pair's names five - "ASR 9922, ASR 9912, ASR 9910, ASR 9906 and ASR 9904" - so the two are not interchangeable even though they share an envelope. A component that declares what it fits is a better source than a chassis deciding what it will take
provenance.four-port-100ge: datasheet - c78-740092's "Chassis compatibility" row: "Compatible with the Cisco ASR 9006, ASR 9010, ASR 9904, ASR 9906, ASR 9910, ASR 9912, and ASR 9922 chassis". All seven, stated outright, and the component's own attrs.chassis carries the same list. At 41.4 mm it fits every line card bay in the family. Added to the line card slots only - a compatibility row names a chassis, not a slot, and this chassis's RSP and RP positions take supervisors
provenance.grounding: datasheet - "Bottom rear right side of the chassis", b-asr9k-hardware-installation-guide.pdf p125, in a row that covers the ASR 9010 and the ASR 9910 together, illustrated by Figure 132
provenance.lifecycle: datasheet - searched. No end-of-sale or end-of-life notice for this chassis was found
provenance.no-chassis-power-figure: NOTE, and NARROWED. The current Table 14 says only to use the Cisco Power Calculator, so there is no chassis-level figure for THIS chassis in any document held and the module total here is a floor. That is narrower than what an earlier revision of this file claimed: it said Cisco publishes no chassis draw for ANY ASR 9000, and that is false. The older Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide (asr9kELCIGbk.pdf, OL-17500-09) states "Power Dissipation 7600 W maximum (Cisco ASR 9010 Router)" and 4556 W maximum for the ASR 9006 in its Table A-1 - a table the current revision deleted. Those two chassis predate this one and no equivalent figure for this model appears in either revision, so this is the vendor being silent about this chassis rather than about the family
provenance.ru: datasheet - 36.70 in / 1.75 = 20.97 RU. The chassis OCCUPIES 21 RU and is built about 0.05 in under it. chassis.height carries the real 932.18 mm and chassis.ru the allocation
provenance.side-and-top-faces: datasheet - NAMED but not dimensioned, and drawn as regions rather than decor for that reason. Figure 12 (the chassis footprint figure in b-asr9k-overview-reference-guide.pdf) shows the top plate outline and the rack mounting brackets, and Figure 75 (the chassis cooling path side view) shows the airflow through the side. Both name what is on those faces; NEITHER dimensions any feature on them, so nothing here carries coordinates. Contrast the ASR 9906, whose HIG Figure 17 gives explicit rail positions at 9.45 in and 5.00 in from the rear and where those rails ARE drawn. The distinction is deliberate: a region says "this is here" and decor says "this is here, at this size, in this place", and only the second needs a dimension behind it
provenance.side-face-labels-say-when-a-position-is-: every region on a side face now states either where the feature sits or that no figure dimensions it. That second half is the point. A region reading only "Vertical rack rail locations" is silent about position, and silence is indistinguishable from a position that was known and not written down - which is exactly how a feature ends up drawn at the wrong end with nothing to contradict it. casa-cards found seven such features across two chassis where the LABEL WAS RIGHT AND THE GEOMETRY WAS WRONG, and lint stayed green because no rule compares the two. Saying "present but not dimensioned" gives a reader the same thing a distance would: a claim to check the drawing against
provenance.slot-id-silkscreen-position: measured, and corrected. The printed slot ID row was first placed at y 650 mm, which was the cage bottom plus a round 10 - a guess, not a measurement - and it put every label INSIDE the card bays once those were resized from the cage opening to the component envelope. The renderer paints a legend under the module that covers it, exactly as the skill warns, so all ten vanished. The text row actually measures 666.60 mm down the body, about 27 mm below the cage, which is both the real position and clear of the bays' 654.88 mm bottom edge. A legend that disappears when a component is placed is in the wrong place, not badly coloured
provenance.slot-pitch-measured-from-the-card-guide-: measured - CORRECTED. An earlier revision of this file described these positions as printed slot IDs. THEY ARE NOT: they are the ten bolt heads on the card guide rail immediately beneath the cage, read at 2400 px. This master DOES print its slot IDs - RSP0, LC0 through LC7, RSP1 - but that text sits about 20 mm further down, outside the window that was scanned. THE NUMBERS ARE UNCHANGED AND ARE THE BETTER OF THE TWO ROWS, which is why they stayed. The bolt centres fall at 28.81, 72.60, 116.29, 160.18, 203.87, 247.76, 291.45, 335.24, 379.03 and 422.82 mm, giving nine pitches of 43.79, 43.69, 43.89, 43.69, 43.89, 43.69, 43.79, 43.79 and 43.79 - a mean of 43.78 with a spread of 0.2 mm. Ten times that is 437.8 against the cage's measured 438.70. The TEXT row measured the same way gives pitches ranging 41.78 to 55.16, because a text label's centre moves with its character count - RSP0 is four characters and LC0 is three - so printed IDs locate a slot only as well as their own width allows. A uniform repeated feature is a better ruler than variable-width text, and the rail is uniform
provenance.slots: datasheet - Figure 22 "Cisco ASR 9910 Router Slot ID Numbering", p37 of b-asr9k-overview-reference-guide.pdf. Left to right on the FRONT: Slot 0 = RSP0, Slot 1 to 8 = Line card 0 to 7, Slot 9 = RSP1. The RSP pair is the OUTER pair, as on the ASR 9906 and unlike the 9904. CAUTION - Figure 22's rear view RUNS OFF THE RIGHT EDGE OF THE PDF PAGE and is clipped, so the fabric slot count is not readable from it. That is a defect in Cisco's own document, not a fetch failure
provenance.stencil-rounds-up: NOTE - the stencil records height_in 3.6750, i.e. 36.75 in, against Table 13's 36.70. The stencil has ROUNDED UP TO THE WHOLE RU (21 x 1.75 = 36.75). Same 0.05 in rounding as the ASR 9906 master. The guide's figure is carried
provenance.the-stencil-masters-are-swapped: READ THIS FIRST. Cisco's Visio master named "ASR-9910 Front" is this chassis's REAR, and the one named "ASR-9910 Rear" is its FRONT. This is not an extraction error - it is in Cisco's own master names. The proof is on the artwork: the master called Front prints FC0 through FC4 beneath its card cage and carries the fan trays and a mesh exhaust, while the master called Rear prints RSP0, LC0 to LC7, RSP1 and carries the cable management tray with the cisco logo. Figure 22 of b-asr9k-overview-reference-guide.pdf settles which is which: it captions the RSP/line-card side "Front View" and shows fabric cards and fan trays on the other side. Anyone modelling this chassis from the stencil by FILENAME will build it back to front. It also cost a wrong number here before it was caught: dividing the fabric cage by ten gave a 38.88 mm slot pitch that did not match the sibling ASR 9906, which is what prompted the check
provenance.twelve-port-100ge: datasheet - c78-737623's "Chassis compatibility" row reads "Compatible with the Cisco ASR 9904, ASR 9910, ASR 9912, and ASR 9922 chassis". This chassis is named, so cisco/a99-12x100ge@1 joins the line card bays. NOTE WHICH CHASSIS IS ABSENT: the ASR 9906. That card goes in every other 9900-generation chassis and not in the 9906, which is the second time a Cisco compatibility row has singled that chassis out, and exactly why these lists are transcribed rather than inferred from generation
provenance.weight: datasheet - Table 13. "Chassis only - 143.11 pounds (64.915 kg)" and "Chassis: Configured with two fan trays, two RSPs, five fabric cards, and one PEM - 349.59 pounds (158.575 kg)"
provenance.width-wording: NOTE - the 9910's Table 13 row reads "17.6 inches (44.70 cm) including chassis rack-mount flanges and front door width", which would make 447 mm the FLANGED width and leave no body figure. The 9912 and 9922 rows give 17.6 as the body and 19.0 as the flanged width on separate lines, and the 9906 row gives a bare 17.6. So the 9910 row most likely has that phrase attached to the wrong number. The gate-1 check settles it independently: calibrating this master's ink box as the 19.0 in rack face and its height as Table 13's 36.70 in gives x and y scales agreeing to 0.00 percent, which they could not if the ink box were 447 mm. 447 is therefore the BODY, and it is carried as such
